cards.text: The LORD gives Moses, Israel's leader, and Aaron the priest a job: count the Kohathites, one of the clans of the Levites. Not every Kohathite, though. Only the men qualified to serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.

cards.question: Which Kohathite men get counted for the work at the Tent of Meeting?

answers.text: Men from thirty to fifty years old
Men from twenty to sixty years old
Men from twelve to forty years old

cards.question: The LORD says the service of the Kohathites at the Tent of Meeting regards the most ___ things.

cards.text: Whenever the camp sets out, Aaron and his sons go in first and take down the veil of the curtain. It's moving day, and not the kind where your buddy shows up two hours late to carry ONE lamp.

cards.question: Aaron and his sons have taken down the veil of the curtain. What do they cover with it?

cards.text: Then they wrap everything piece by piece: the ark, the table of the Presence, the lampstand, the gold altar, the utensils and the bronze altar. Each one gets colored cloth and fine leather, then poles or a carrying frame, and the bread offering even stays right on the table. Friend, I've packed a LOT of cookie boxes, and I have never wrapped anything like this.
When Aaron and his sons finish covering the holy objects, and the camp is ready to move, the Kohathites finally come in.

cards.question: Everything's wrapped and the camp is ready to move. What do the Kohathites come in to do?
The Kohathites can touch the holy objects as long as they're careful.

cards.text: No touching, or they will die. Meanwhile, Eleazar son of Aaron the priest gets a big assignment of his own.

cards.question: Eleazar son of Aaron the priest has oversight of the entire ___ and everything in it.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses and Aaron again: "Do not allow the Kohathite tribal clans to be cut off from among the Levites."

cards.question: The LORD wants the Kohathites to live when they come near the most holy things. What are Aaron and his sons to do for them?

answers.text: Go in and assign each man his task
Teach them to wrap the holy objects
Lead them in carrying only at night

cards.question: The Kohathites may go in and look at the holy objects, as long as it's only for a moment.

cards.text: Not even for a moment, or they will die. Friend, I can't walk past my own oven without peeking through the glass, and these men carry the most holy things without ONE look.
Next the LORD tells Moses to count the Gershonites, same ages as the Kohathites: thirty to fifty. The LORD is consistent, and me? I can't even make two batches of cookies come out the same.

cards.question: The Kohathites carry the holy objects. What do the Gershonites carry?

cards.text: Tabernacle curtains, courtyard curtains, entrance curtains, the fine leather covering and the ropes. If it folds, it's a Gershonite job.

cards.question: The Gershonites decide for themselves what each man carries.

cards.text: Their duties are under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest. Then come the sons of Merari, counted by their clans, thirty to fifty years old.

cards.question: The Kohathites have the holy objects and the Gershonites have the curtains. What do the Merarites carry?

cards.text: Frames, crossbars, posts, bases, tent pegs and ropes, and you know the friend who vanishes the SECOND the big stuff comes off the truck? Not these guys.

cards.question: The Merarites have a lot of pieces to haul. How do they know which items are theirs to carry?

answers.text: Each item is assigned by name
Each man picks what he wants

cards.question: The Merarites work under the direction of Ithamar, the same son of Aaron who directs the Gershonites.

cards.text: Then Moses, Aaron and the leaders do the counting, clan by clan. The Kohathites come to 2,750, the Gershonites to 2,630 and the Merarites to 3,200, for a total of 8,580 men. I lose count of chocolate chips somewhere around seven.

cards.question: At the LORD's command through Moses, each man counted was assigned his ___ and burden.

cards.text: Every man, every job, just as the LORD commanded Moses. And friend, after years in the back of a junk drawer, I know EXACTLY what it feels like to finally get handed a job.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the wrapping list, the cloth/leather/poles detail with the bread offering, and the cookie-box joke. Only the opening card may run to 3 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "Meanwhile" ties Eleazar's oversight in time to the Kohathites' carrying. Numbers 4:16 doesn't say how the two connect or when.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The setup line "The Kohathites carry the holy objects" rules out the wrong answer "The altars and lampstand." Stop 1 already showed the baker that those are the holy objects the Kohathites carry. That leaves a two-way pick.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The setup line "The Kohathites have the holy objects and the Gershonites have the curtains" rules out both wrong answers. "The lamps and oil" and "The bowls and pitchers" are holy objects the baker already saw wrapped for the Kohathites (Numbers 4:7, 9). That leaves only the right answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This census summary card has three sentences: who counts, the clan totals with the grand total, and the chocolate-chip joke.
